raiseHistory.measurementCorrections: Two harness defects were counted into the 422 and are gone from the 1326. (1) Body-portal leakage: a surface that portals to document.body (an anchored panel, a phone sheet, a menu, a picker) was left attached when the next scenario mounted, so every scenario after it measured its controls too. The lanes mount all scenarios into one page, so leftovers accumulated: by the tenth panel scenario the body carried ten stacked panels, and which of them survived depended on production's own mutual exclusion, which made the total non-deterministic (1457, 1471, 1558, 1584, 1601, 1623 across six runs of the same tree, and 419/429/429 across three runs of the pre-existing 31 alone — the recorded 422 sat inside that band, so the gate it guarded was already decided by timing). render-assertion-harness.ts now sweeps every body child a mount added, after the named closes it already ran, at the start of the next mount — late enough that a capture still photographs the surface its own scenario opened. Three passes over the same page now return 1326, 1326, 1326, and two independent runs of touch-targets.mjs return 1326 and 1326. It removed the double-counted db-toggle-switch (10 -> 6 on the pre-existing set) and db-view-config-number (12 -> 4). (2) Harness-only anchors: the hidden button this harness creates for a popover to position against is not a product control, and eleven more of them arrived with the new surfaces. They are now spans, which the lane's interactive selector does not match, and the three T028 wrote inline (db-calendar-options-trigger, db-calendar-timeline-options-trigger, db-chart-options-trigger, 1 each) fold into the same helper and drop to 0.
raiseHistory.verification: Attributed per scenario by tagging each ScenarioSpec with its own unique name rather than scenarioLabel() (which collides for scenarios sharing a renderer/bag pair) and summing that run's under-floor rows per class, the same method T029's entry describes. The 871 the new scenarios add: 558 db-multi-select-remove (72 per table-rendering capture scenario, 86 in the full-palette one, 24 in the footer variant's shorter row set, 16 in the grouped table), 141 more db-table-footer-trigger (16 per new table scenario, 13 in the footer variant), 51 unclassed buttons and inputs (32 in the column manager at 24x24, 10 in the select-cell editor, 4 in the sort panel, 3 view-config checkboxes at 13x13, 2 view-config buttons at 121x24), 48 clickable-icon in the column manager, 18 db-record-icon, 16 db-color-picker-swatch at 18x18, 5 each of db-list-group-new, db-gallery-group-new and db-option-delete, 4 db-view-tab, 4 more mini-calendar buttons from the two date-picker scenarios, and single findings in the search, filter, record-body and icon-picker surfaces. Every pre-existing class holds its exact prior count except the six the measurement corrections above explain. unstyled-links.mjs over the same 73 scenarios: 1548 links, 0 resolving to a user-agent colour, PASS, identical across two runs. No styles.css or src/views change accompanies this raise.
raiseHistory.productFindings: Every count here is a real shortfall, not an allowance. Three are newly visible because no fixture and no pre-043 constructed scenario ever mounted the surface: db-multi-select-remove (the per-tag remove button inside a multi-select cell, the largest single population here — it repeats once per tag per row, so a capture-sized 18-row table already shows 72 of them), db-file-tag-remove (10x14, the smallest control this pass has ever measured, the per-tag remove button on the file.tags pseudo-column), and the column manager's 48 clickable-icon plus 32 unclassed 24x24 buttons, which are that panel's per-row controls. db-color-picker-swatch at 18x18 and the view-config panel's 13x13 checkbox inputs are the two other honest misses. None is fixed here: resizing a product control is the same operator-scale decision this file's own `why` and `lastTriage` describe, and it would move captures this packet is not scoped to move.

note: The constructed pass first ran against no baseline at all (2026-09-03) and measured 8503 under-floor controls across 12 classes, red before any fix or declaration existed. Five of the twelve were newly discovered here — invisible to the fixture pass because no scenarios.mjs fixture mounts them: db-row-insert-button (22x22, 3998 instances — the table's hover-to-insert-row button, repeated at every row gap in the 2000-row bench table), db-gallery-card-open (24x24, 3200 instances — the gallery card's open button), db-timeline-mobile-menu-button (22x22, 960 instances — the timeline's phone-only overflow menu button, ironically missing the floor its own name promises), db-board-pagination-dot (12x12, 10 instances) and db-calendar-week-allday-more (67x13, 16 instances). db-board-pagination-dot is declared, not counted here: its `::before` inset is -16px on every side of a 12px dot, a 44px effective hit area a bounding box does not see (styles.css:19696-19699), the same shape as the checkbox exemption in touch-targets.mjs's DECLARED list, which now names it. The remaining four (8493 = 8503 - 10) were real, recorded here rather than fixed. A fix was drafted and verified for three of them the first time this pass ran, then reverted rather than landed because landing it would have invalidated the sourceHashes on eight unrelated census/audit artefacts (cascade-audit, checkbox-appearance, checkbox-inventory, design-conformance, engine-parity, surface-census, token-census, view-census); re-stamping surfaced that two of the eight — checkbox-appearance (a pre-existing 2.99:1 border-contrast shortfall on a board-drop-language fixture) and engine-parity (pre-existing Chrome/WebKit width differences, 520 vs 512, on unrelated fixtures) — fail for reasons that predate any touch-target work, confirmed by running both against the untouched tree: identical failing output. Those two remain a different scope's problem (WCAG contrast and cross-engine tolerance, not touch targets) and are recorded unchanged rather than fixed incidentally. This time the fix was landed: see `lastTriage` above for the applied change, the per-class before/after count, and the verification that produced them. db-calendar-week-allday-more (67x13, a real `<button>` inside the week/day all-day overflow row) was never a fix candidate for this pass regardless: raising its height sits inside the calendar's CSS-grid all-day row track (`grid-row` positioning shared with event-segment bars), an area this program's own history already flags as fragile (the runtime-vars.css calendar-formula finding), so it stays deferred pending a dedicated pass with its own capture verification. The other 7 recurring classes (db-calendar-month-segment 200, db-calendar-more-events 56, db-calendar-week-allday-date 16, db-table-footer-trigger 32, db-timeline-create-button 1, db-timeline-nav-button 12, db-timeline-scale-menu 2 — 319 total) are the same shortfalls the fixture baseline already tracks, now also counted at the scale a real renderer repeats them; 319 + db-calendar-week-allday-more's 16 = 335, the new baseline.
